high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates as of July 24 at MB, Sacombank, HDBank, Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank, and Others
high.summary: A survey of online deposit rates as of July 24 reveals continued and significant divergence across Vietnam's banking system. The highest advertised rate stands at **7.8% per annum for 12-month deposits**, offered by ACB, which also quotes 7.6% for 6-month and 7.7% for 9-month tenors. A total of **7 banks are now offering 7% or above** for 12-month deposits, including Saigonbank (7.2%), Bac A Bank (7.1%), MBV, VCBNeo, VIB, and PGBank (all at 7.0%). Notably, MBV and VCBNeo maintain a flat 7.0% curve across 6-, 9-, 12-, and 18-month maturities.

high.title: Bank Deposit Interest Rates on July 25 at MB, Sacombank, HDBank, Agribank, Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank and Others
high.summary: As of July 25, Vietnamese bank deposit rates continue to show significant divergence, particularly at tenors of 6 months and above. The spread between the highest and lowest 12-month deposit rates across surveyed banks has widened to a notable 4.1 percentage points — ranging from 7.8% per annum down to 3.7% per annum. ACB leads the pack at 7.8%/year for 12-month deposits, followed by Saigonbank at 7.2% and Bac A Bank at 7.1%. MBV, VCBNeo, VIB, and PGBank cluster around the 7.0% level for 12-month tenors.

medium.title: First Bank to Report a Loss in Q2/2026: Saigonbank Posts Decline Across All Business Lines
medium.summary:
Saigonbank (SGB) has become the first Vietnamese commercial bank to report a loss in Q2/2026, flagging stress in a segment of the banking sector that warrants monitoring. Net interest income — the bank's primary revenue driver — collapsed 31.34% year-on-year to VND 160 billion, while net foreign exchange trading income fell a sharp 40.45% to just VND 2.5 billion. Operating costs simultaneously rose 10.19% to VND 168.5 billion, squeezing pre-provision profit by 79.49% to only VND 23.7 billion. Pressure intensified further as the bank was forced to increase credit loss provisions by 62.38% to VND 63.7 billion. While Saigonbank is a small institution and not systemically significant, its results are a leading indicator of broader credit quality deterioration and margin compression across the sector. The significant drop in FX trading income may reflect reduced VND/USD volatility or tighter spreads. Fund managers should watch whether larger, systemically important banks report similar NIM compression and provision spikes when Q2 earnings are released in coming weeks, as this could influence SBV's stance on lending rate guidance.

medium.title: State Bank of Vietnam Clarifies the 24-Hour Waiting Period for Online Transfers Exceeding VND 400 Million
medium.summary:
The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) has issued a public clarification via Official Dispatch No. 6190 regarding new regulations on large-value online fund transfers. The SBV confirmed that the **mandatory 24-hour waiting period does not apply universally** to all transfers above VND 400 million (~USD 15,600). Instead, the cooling-off period applies specifically to transfers made to **new beneficiary accounts** or transactions exceeding a customer's self-registered transaction limit. A **default limit of VND 400 million with a minimum 24-hour hold** will be applied to customers who do not proactively register their own limits. Banks must complete implementation by **March 1, 2027**. While primarily a consumer protection and anti-fraud measure, this regulation has indirect implications for institutional liquidity management and intraday fund flows within the banking system, which fixed income and FX market participants should factor into settlement and operational planning.
